title: Dashed outer lines on the ring road (east)
description: On Route 1, the ring road circling the whole country, the outer lines are dashed only in the eastern part (roughly from just east of Akureyri round to Höfn), while in the west they are full. Near intersections and in towns the outer lines are usually full everywhere, so this does not work close to intersections.

title: Google car with a large black box (eastern highlands)
description: On the eastern highland roads marked in black on the map (F88 south from the ring road, and the Jökuldalur road 923 / F910), a large black box is visible on the rear of the Google car.

title: Google car with a red box (south-east, towards Höfn)
description: On the roads marked in red on the map (the ring road along the south-east coast towards Höfn), some kind of red box is visible at the rear left of the Google car.

title: Street name endings by neighbourhood (capital region)
description: In basically every town, street name endings are determined by the area: in the neighbourhood of Bakkar in Reykjavík, for example, the street names end in 'bakki'. Neighbourhoods are not always marked on the map, but the street name endings let you scan the town for an area that ends similarly. The smallest residential roads follow this pattern; bigger roads usually end in 'vegur' or 'braut', and 'gata' is most common in the city centres. The map shows most of the endings in the capital region.

title: Street name endings by neighbourhood (Selfoss)
description: As everywhere in Iceland, the street name endings in Selfoss are determined by the neighbourhood (Hólar, Heiði, Tún, Vellir, Land…): find a street, then look for the area of town whose small residential streets end the same way.

title: Street name endings by neighbourhood (Akureyri)
description: As everywhere in Iceland, the street name endings in Akureyri are determined by the neighbourhood (Síða, Hlíð, Gil, Gerði, Lundur, Tún, Hagi…): find a street, then look for the area of town whose small residential streets end the same way.

title: Alphabetical street names in Fossvogur
description: Within a neighbourhood the street names are sometimes also in alphabetical order. In Fossvogur (Reykjavík) all the street names end in 'land'; in the west they start with the letter A and going east the names come in clumps in alphabetical order. The order is not always west to east — it can run in a circle or any shape — but streets starting with the same letter are often close to each other.

title: Akureyri bus stops: yellow signs and unique shelters
description: Akureyri has unique yellow signs for its bus stops, and three types of shelters that are all unique to Akureyri. The yellow circles on the glass shelters are unique to Akureyri as well.

title: Glass bus shelters with black birds (Fjarðabyggð)
description: Glass bus shelters with black birds on them are only found in the far eastern towns of Neskaupstaður, Eskifjörður, Reyðarfjörður and Fáskrúðsfjörður.

title: Unpainted metal sheet bus shelters
description: Unpainted metal sheet shelters are found in Hafnarfjörður, Garður and Sandgerði. On the glass side they often carry the coat of arms of their municipality (a lighthouse for Hafnarfjörður), although in Hafnarfjörður some have none.

title: Gray bus shelters with yellow window trims (Hafnarfjörður)
description: Gray shelters with yellow window trims are only found in Hafnarfjörður.

title: Glass bus shelters with blue lines (Akranes)
description: Glass shelters with blue lines going across the glass are unique to Akranes.

title: Round-roofed red metal sheet bus shelters
description: Round-roofed red metal sheet shelters are found both in Reykjavík and in the larger towns of the Reykjanes peninsula (one was also found in Sauðárkrókur, but that is extremely rare).

title: Triangle-roofed red bus shelters and red signs (Reykjanes)
description: Red metal sheet shelters with a triangle roof are only found on the Reykjanes peninsula (Keflavík, Njarðvík, Sandgerði). The red bus stop signs are unique to Keflavík and Njarðvík.

title: Green metal sheet bus shelters
description: Green sheet metal shelters are found all around Kópavogur and Mosfellsbær, along with the Álftanes peninsula. There is also one in Seltjarnarnes.

title: Green glass bus shelters (capital region)
description: This green shelter is the most common type of bus shelter. 99% of the time it is found in the capital region, but it can rarely be seen in Keflavík, and one was found in Borgarnes.

title: Green glass bus shelters with white dots (Kópavogur)
description: Green glass shelters with white dots are completely unique to Kópavogur.

title: Gray/white bus shelters (eastern Reykjavík)
description: These gray/white shelters are only found in the eastern parts of Reykjavík, where they are quite common.

title: Blue bins in Bolungarvík
description: Bolungarvík is the only place with blue bins apart from the capital region. There are always two blue bins together, sometimes with a gray bin alongside them.

title: Westfjords recycling stickers with a white bar on top
description: In the Westfjords, the recycling stickers have a white bar on top of the waste icon; this is unique to these bins. On the infographic: Patreksfjörður, Tálknafjörður, Bíldudalur, Flateyri and Suðureyri.

title: Two black bins with white and green stickers (Ísafjörður area)
description: Usually two, rarely three black bins with an alternate style of recycling sticker, white and green. On the infographic: Ísafjörður, Hnífsdalur, Þingeyri, Flateyri and Suðureyri.

title: Bins with the Snæfellsbær coat of arms (Ólafsvík, Rif)
description: Two black bins, one of which has a green lid. Several west-coast towns have this setup; what tells them apart is the coat of arms on the bin, often small and hard to see. Here, the Snæfellsbær coat of arms (Ólafsvík and Rif).

title: Bins with the Borgarbyggð coat of arms (Borgarnes, Hvanneyri)
description: Two black bins, one of which has a green lid, with the Borgarbyggð coat of arms (Borgarnes and Hvanneyri). Similar bins exist in other west-coast towns, and on the north coast with different coats of arms or logos: check the coat of arms.

title: Bins with the Akranes coat of arms
description: Two black bins, one of which has a green lid, with the Akranes coat of arms (it can be very faded and appear empty). Similar bins exist in other west-coast towns: check the coat of arms.

title: Stykkishólmur bins: small white coat of arms
description: The Stykkishólmur bins look very similar to the common green/gray/brown ones; the difference is the small white coat of arms on the black/gray bin.

title: Blue bins: capital region or Bolungarvík
description: The capital region is the only place, along with Bolungarvík in the Westfjords, where you will find blue bins.

title: Reykjavík bins: coat of arms with two pillars
description: Reykjavík bins are very easy to recognise by the large coat of arms with two pillars in front of waves.

title: Kópavogur bins: coat of arms
description: Kópavogur bins carry their coat of arms. From a distance it is best recognised by the white arrow-looking shape at the top.

title: Garðabær bins: black/gray, no coat of arms
description: Garðabær bins are all black/gray and have no coat of arms on them.

title: Hafnarfjörður bins: one blue bin
description: Hafnarfjörður bins are similar to the Garðabær ones (black/gray, no coat of arms), but one of them is blue.

title: Seltjarnarnes bins: letter 'i' coat of arms
description: Seltjarnarnes bins are black and carry the Seltjarnarnes coat of arms, which looks like a large letter 'i'.

title: Mosfellsbær bins: triangle coat of arms
description: Mosfellsbær bins have a triangle-looking coat of arms, made of three parts.

title: Keflavík bins: waste stickers without white parts
description: Keflavík bins have the colourful waste stickers, but what is unique there is that the stickers have no white part on top or at the bottom. They also often carry one of the two logos found all around the peninsula. On the infographic: Keflavík and Njarðvík.

title: Grindavík bins: coat of arms
description: Grindavík often has its own coat of arms on the bins, but sometimes they just carry one of the two logos found all around the Reykjanes peninsula.

title: Reykjanes peninsula bin logos
description: Two logos are found on bins all around the Reykjanes peninsula: an 'S', or maybe a road-looking shape with a line through it, and a weird shape that looks a bit like a Japanese letter. On the infographic: Garður, Sandgerði, Hafnir, Vogar, Grindavík, Keflavík and Njarðvík.

title: South Iceland bins: black with a blue lid
description: In the south, bins are most often black with a blue lid.

title: Vestmannaeyjabær bins
description: The colours of the bins in Vestmannaeyjabær vary a lot, but as a general rule one is black/gray, one is green or has a green lid, and one is brown or has a brown lid.

title: Árborg bins: river coat of arms
description: Bins in the Árborg region carry the regional coat of arms, which looks like a river meandering through a landscape (Selfoss, Eyrarbakki, Stokkseyri).

title: Black bins with a white circular logo north of Selfoss
description: The area roughly north of Selfoss has black bins with a white circular logo, one of them usually with a blue lid. The white circular logo can be found in many other places as well though, mainly along the north coast.

title: Hella and Hvolsvöllur bins: regional coats of arms
description: Hella and Hvolsvöllur have their respective regional coats of arms (Rangárþing ytra and Rangárþing eystra) on their bins.

title: Þorlákshöfn bins: plain gray and black with blue lid
description: Þorlákshöfn bins are often just a gray one and a black one with a blue lid, generally with no markings or stickers.

title: Höfn bins: green, sometimes with a large white sticker
description: Höfn bins are usually just green, sometimes with a large white sticker on them. In Gen 4 coverage you can also sometimes see the blue and white coat of arms.

title: Djúpivogur bins: white sticker behind the waste stickers
description: Djúpivogur bins can be recognised by the white rectangular sticker behind the colourful waste stickers.

title: Breiðdalsvík bins: green/gray/brown with the white sticker
description: Breiðdalsvík bins have the common green/gray/brown colours, but they basically always have the east coast white sticker. This separates them from the regular green/gray/brown bins, since elsewhere the white sticker is rarer.

title: Green bins on the roadside (western Fáskrúðsfjörður)
description: Unique to the western half of Fáskrúðsfjörður: green bins standing on the side of the road.

title: Four bins in Egilsstaðir and Seyðisfjörður
description: Shown on the guide's infographic only (not described in its text): Egilsstaðir and Seyðisfjörður have four bins together — black, green, brown and black — each with a colourful waste sticker.

title: Hvammstangi bins: polar bear coat of arms
description: In Gen 4 coverage, Hvammstangi bins have a coat of arms with two polar bears on it. In Gen 3 they are just normal single green bins with no coat of arms.

title: Skagaströnd bins: two black, green lid, white circular logo
description: Skagaströnd has two black bins, one with a green lid, and a circular white logo.

title: Skagafjörður bins: small blue coat of arms
description: Bins in the Skagafjörður region always have a small blue coat of arms. It can look similar to the Reykjavík one, but it has a sword on the left side and no waves in the background. On the infographic: Sauðárkrókur, Hofsós, Hólar and Varmahlíð.

title: Siglufjörður and Ólafsfjörður bins
description: Siglufjörður and Ólafsfjörður have the common green/gray/brown bins in Gen 3. In Gen 4 they have three or four bins of varying colours with the colourful waste stickers (not very recognisable).

title: Akureyri bins with a large white sticker bottom (north-west)
description: Akureyri has two types of bins. On the north-west side of town: black bins with the colourful waste stickers — in Akureyri the white part at the bottom of the sticker is larger than usual.

title: Akureyri bins: black with a circular logo
description: Akureyri has two types of bins: in most of the town, black bins with a circular logo (the north-west side has black bins with colourful waste stickers instead).

title: Dalvíkurbyggð bins: two black, coat of arms
description: Bins in Dalvíkurbyggð usually come in pairs of two black bins, one with a green lid, with the coat of arms of the region and either a large or a small alternate style recycling sticker. On the infographic: Dalvík, Árskógssandur/Hauganes and Hjalteyri.

title: Grenivík bins: like Dalvíkurbyggð without a coat of arms
description: Grenivík bins are similar to the Dalvíkurbyggð ones (two black bins, one with a green lid) but have no coat of arms on them.

title: Svalbarðseyri bins: metallic bin alongside
description: Svalbarðseyri has a black bin with a green lid, along with either a metallic bin (cubic or round) or sometimes another black bin.

title: Reykjahlíð bins: three black, green and blue lids
description: Reykjahlíð has three black bins, one with a green lid and one with a blue lid. They also carry the circular white logo.

title: Húsavík bins: single black with a white circular logo
description: Húsavík has single black bins with the white circular logo.

title: Kópasker bins: round metallic bins
description: Kópasker has round metallic bins, or sometimes normal single black bins.

title: Raufarhöfn bins: one brown and three black
description: Raufarhöfn has four bins: a brown one and three black ones. One of the black ones has a green lid and one a blue lid. Only the brown bin has a colourful recycling sticker.

title: Common green/gray/brown bins
description: The common green/gray/brown bins (often with a thumbs-up logo) are found in Grundarfjörður, Hveragerði, Siglufjörður, Ólafsfjörður, Þórshöfn, Bakkafjörður, and in Neskaupstaður, Eskifjörður, Reyðarfjörður, Fáskrúðsfjörður and Stöðvarfjörður.

title: Single plain black bins
description: Single plain black bins are found in Búðardalur, Blönduós, Flúðir, Vopnafjörður and Bakkagerði.

title: Dark blue fire hydrants (southern capital region)
description: Dark blue fire hydrants are only found in the southern part of the capital region (Kópavogur, Garðabær, Hafnarfjörður) in Gen 4; in older coverage the colours are different. Blue hydrants with a gray top part are not unique to this area — they are very common all around the country.

title: Hydrant marker poles with a curved brace (Húsavík)
description: Egilsstaðir and Húsavík both have uniquely shaped marker poles on their hydrants. The colour can vary but the shape is always the same: in Húsavík, a pole with a curved brace.

title: L-shaped hydrant marker poles (Egilsstaðir)
description: Egilsstaðir and Húsavík both have uniquely shaped marker poles on their hydrants. The colour can vary but the shape is always the same: in Egilsstaðir, a pole bent at a right angle near its base.

title: Tall green pipe heads (Egilsstaðir)
description: These tall, green pipe heads are unique to Egilsstaðir.

title: Ásbrú, the former base near Keflavík airport
description: The Ásbrú area near Keflavík airport is very easy to recognise. There is only Gen 3 coverage. The buildings are mainly long, pale apartment blocks with red, green or blue roofs. Yellow hydrants with a black bottom are unique to this area, and the large red and white water tower can often be seen from a distance.

title: Yellow-red-yellow marker poles on electric boxes (north and east)
description: On electric boxes, alternating yellow, red, yellow marker poles are only found on the north and east coasts — notably not in Akureyri. By far most common in the north-east, though one was found in Grundarfjörður.

title: Orange-tipped marker poles on electric boxes (Akureyri)
description: Orange-tipped marker poles on electric boxes are completely unique to Akureyri and found on almost every box, which makes them a very good clue for the city.

title: Black-yellow-black marker poles on electric boxes (Reykjanes)
description: Alternating black, yellow, black marker poles on electric boxes are only found on the Reykjanes peninsula. Do not confuse them with yellow, black, yellow poles, which are found all over the country.

title: Electric box numbers by area (Reykjavík)
description: The first two digits of the number on electric boxes in Reykjavík and parts of the surrounding municipalities correspond to a specific area (10xxx Seltjarnarnes, 11xxx–13xxx Reykjavík from west to east, 14xxx–15xxx Kópavogur/Breiðholt). The numbers are often hard to see, and some boxes in this area do not use this format.

title: Electric box numbers 15xxx and 16xxx (Ísafjörður, Bolungarvík)
description: The town of Ísafjörður also uses the electric box number format, with 15xxx, and Bolungarvík uses 16xxx — so check whether you are even in the capital area before reading a 15xxx number.
